description: We are a two-member team comprising Dhwani Gupta and Adarsh, developing the Space Mission Design Game for NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project aims to transform space exploration into an immersive, interactive learning experience, allowing players to step into the shoes of an astronaut. Through realistic mission scenarios, engaging minigames, and problem-solving challenges, we aspire to make space science accessible, exciting, and experiential.

Players explore a station environment, complete an equipment inspection, take part in a Daily Planning Conference, and carry out a guided BIO-LAB activity involving simulated plant-growth medium pH readings and adjustment.

details:
ORBITALIS — A Day in the Orbit is an interactive, browser-based astronaut experience that simulates a day aboard the International Space Station (ISS). Players step into the role of an astronaut and progress through different activities, beginning with an ISS orientation and equipment inspection, followed by a Daily Planning Conference (DPC), and concluding with scientific experimentation in the BIO-LAB.

The experience combines an interactive station environment with task-based gameplay. During the BIO-LAB activity, players examine a simulated plant-growth medium pH reading, classify it and make an appropriate adjustment to reach a target range. The experiment demonstrates a simplified scientific process, with illustrative values rather than real sensor measurements.

ORBITALIS aims to make human spaceflight and research aboard the ISS more approachable through interactive learning. It introduces players to astronaut responsibilities, mission planning, scientific experimentation and the relationship between space operations, ground support and scientific users. Its educational framework also incorporates NASA's four-segment science-mission framework: Launch, Space, Ground and User, with a reference to the original NASA resource.

The project was developed using the PlayCanvas Engine, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with a browser-based deployment. Rather than relying on a large, resource-intensive 3D simulation, we focused on an interactive, interface-driven experience with a lightweight visual environment, responsive controls and cinematic transitions.

Our creative approach was to present a simulated day in orbit as a connected experience rather than a collection of isolated educational screens. Throughout development, we considered accessibility, usability, mobile compatibility, performance, clarity of instructions, scientific context and the distinction between real-world NASA research and simulated gameplay.

Developed by Team IntelEvo, ORBITALIS seeks to inspire curiosity about life in space and make space-based scientific research more engaging and understandable.
